memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I have seen these people,' the Lord said to Moses, 'and they are a stiff-necked people. Now leave me alone so that my anger may burn against them and that I may destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation.'" - Exod 32:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Stiff-necked" is a farming picture. It describes an ox that refuses the yoke, jerking its head away from the farmer's direction. Not weak — stubborn. Not confused — resistant.

That is a diagnosis, and it applies far beyond Israel. There are areas where each of us knows exactly what God has said and still pulls our head the other way.

God's anger here is real and right. This is not divine temper; it is holy opposition to evil. A God who shrugged at idolatry and betrayal would not be loving — He would be indifferent.

But listen to the extraordinary phrase: "Now leave me alone." Why would God say that to a man? It is, in effect, an open door. God is signalling that intercession is possible. He does not need Moses' permission, yet He invites Moses' prayer. This is the God who told Abraham what He was about to do at Sodom (Gen 18:17) — a God who makes room for pleading.

Here we see a shadow of something greater. Jesus does not merely stand at the foot of the mountain; He is our great High Priest who always lives to intercede for us (Heb 7:25). Because of Him, we approach the throne of grace with confidence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you being stiff-necked with God right now?
2. Do you believe that God genuinely welcomes your prayers for others?
3. Who has God placed on your heart to intercede for this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, bend my stubborn heart to Your good yoke. Thank You that Jesus lives to pray for me even now. Amen.
